stop_status: REPAIRED - two high-severity memory-safety defects (unbounded i2d_X509 writes in both certificate flights; 32-byte HMAC tail for the application-chosen ticket digest) were found and fixed. Focused BATCH and ASan controls pass. Nothing is promoted to SAFETY_DISCHARGED or SAFE_COMPATIBLE.

authority.abi: C ABI unchanged; no export, signature, #[repr(C)] layout, method-table slot, exported symbol or CRYPTO_* seam coordinate changed.
external_contracts: A C caller passes live object pointers to every exported entry point; a stale or double-released pointer is outside the C contract. Reference counts turn a destructor-time reentrant release into a defined no-op (REF_DESTROYING), not an arbitrary stale-pointer detector.

A transferred object (BIO, X509_STORE, CTLOG_STORE, EVP_PKEY, SSL_SESSION, X509 chain) carries exactly one owned reference; the set0 transfer consumes it and the caller must not also release it. Passing the incumbent pointer as the new transfer is a caller contract violation (authority parity; latent self-alias recorded, not reproduced as a new obligation).

An application callback (client_hello_cb, servername_cb, alpn_select_cb, ticket_key_cb, msg_callback, ex_data free callbacks) must not free or invalidate the SSL/SSL_CTX it receives. Callback pointers are raw and stored verbatim; arguments are application-owned.

Handshake input is a length-delimited byte slice; every field read is checked against the slice bounds. The reduced server does not model several authority length policy checks (recorded divergences).
ticket_key_cb initialises the supplied EVP_CIPHER_CTX and HMAC_CTX. The IV is bounded by EVP_MAX_IV_LENGTH and the MAC by EVP_MAX_MD_SIZE; the authority reserves EVP_MAX_MD_SIZE for the MAC.

boundaries.mechanism: object ownership model: OwnedCtx/RawCtx/CtxDestroy, SSL_CTX_new_ex, SSL_new, cert_new, ssl_cert_dup, cert_free
residuals: Every constructor/free is unsafe extern C and requires a live or owned caller pointer; the returned object is owned by the caller.
OwnedCtx::from_raw and release_block remain unsafe proofs; their callers are internal and each is a single release.
Constructors deliberately skip the destructor on the authority's pre-live refusal arms and release exactly the members acquired so far; the DTLS d1 leak on the ex_data refusal is fixed.

boundaries.mechanism: refcount lifecycle and reentrancy: SSL_CTX_up_ref/free, SSL_up_ref/free, SSL_dup fast path, ex_data free callbacks
residuals: up_ref/free dereference a caller-guaranteed live pointer; there is no NULL check (authority parity).
The destructor runs with the count at REF_DESTROYING; a reentrant free is a defined no-op, while any other reentrant use observes partially torn-down state.
The caller must own the reference it releases; an arbitrary stale pointer is not detected.

boundaries.mechanism: ownership transfers: SSL_set_SSL_CTX, SSL_CTX_set_cert_store/set1_cert_store, SSL_CTX_set0_ctlog_store, SSL_set0_tmp_dh_pkey, SSL_set_bio/set0_rbio/set0_wbio, SSL_set_fd/wfd/rfd
residuals: SSL_CTX_set_cert_store, SSL_CTX_set0_ctlog_store and SSL_set0_tmp_dh_pkey free then store the same field; passing the incumbent as the transferred pointer is a caller contract violation (authority parity, latent self-alias).
SSL_set_SSL_CTX assigns ssl->ctx after SSL_CTX_free(old); an ex_data free callback that re-enters and reads ssl->ctx in that window observes the old pointer (authority parity).
Transferred BIO references and the rbio == wbio two-slot rule are caller obligations; a refused BIO_up_ref would leak the freshly created BIO (unreachable for a live BIO).
SSL_set_fd/wfd/rfd adopt the descriptor with BIO_NOCLOSE; the caller must not close or reuse it while the BIO lives.

boundaries.mechanism: member-buffer/member-slot mediation: MemberBufSlot, MemberCStrSlot, SSL_new/SSL_dup copies, psk_identity_hint, serverinfo, cert-type/ALPN/hostname/pha/ticket members
residuals: MemberBufSlot::store's emptiness precondition is a debug_assert; release builds rely on every caller clearing first.
supportedgroups remains an element-counted raw boundary with three accesses and two destructor frees, bounded by tls1_set_groups (<= 64 entries).
The (ptr,len) pairs stay raw #[repr(C)] fields; validity is an internal constructor invariant, not a type-level one.

boundaries.mechanism: session/certificate/chain accessors and DANE/CT: SSL_get0/1_peer_certificate, SSL_get_peer_cert_chain, SSL_get0_verified_chain, SSL_get0_peer_rpk, dane_tlsa_add/dane_final/ssl_dane_dup
residuals: Peer certificate, verified chain and RPK pointers are borrowed and expire on the next mutation or free.
Session ownership internals live in ssl_sess.rs (rank 61, deferred); this is an unresolved dependency for the session family.
Certificate/chain loaders live in ssl_rsa.rs; their transfer contracts are not re-audited in this batch.

boundaries.mechanism: ClientHello publication and readers: s->clienthello, SSL_client_hello_get0_* and get1_extensions_present/get_extension_order/get0_ext
residuals: The readers are valid only during client_hello_cb; outside it s->clienthello is NULL and they return 0/empty.
The published message points into the caller's handshake slice for the callback duration; the callback must not retain it.

boundaries.mechanism: callback/ex_data setters: verify, msg, cert, client_hello, keylog, PSK, ALPN/NPN, servername, ticket, record padding, async, early data, CT validation
residuals: Raw function pointers and arguments are stored verbatim; the application owns the argument and must not free the SSL/SSL_CTX from a destructor-time callback.
CRYPTO_set_ex_data can replace a slot without a callback; the free callback observes the value current at destruction.

boundaries.mechanism: DANE record/context lifecycle: dane_ctx_enable/final, tlsa_free/DanetlsRecord destroy_body, dane_tlsa_add, ssl_dane_dup
residuals: tlsa data is readable for dlen; the record owns a copy and releases it at the authority site.
trecs ordering indexes dctx->mdord by the validated matching type; the digest table is allocated for DANETLS_MATCHING_LAST + 1.

boundaries.mechanism: reduced lifecycle bodies: SSL_clear, SSL_copy_session_id, SSL_dup
residuals: SSL_clear is a method guard only (no reset) and SSL_copy_session_id copies security attributes rather than sharing the certificate container; both are documented reductions.
SSL_dup up-refs the same object when not quiescent and duplicates it when quiescent; the caller owns one reference in both arms.

boundaries.mechanism: server transition surface: read/write transitions and max_message_size
residuals: Transition writes are reached only with a live connection; an unknown state calls ossl_statem_fatal.

boundaries.mechanism: ClientHello parse: tls_process_client_hello, extension walk, PSK/key-share/ALPN/SNI extraction
residuals: hs must be the full handshake message; every read is bounds-checked against it before use.
A missing supported_groups extension is not rejected by the reduced parser (recorded divergence from SSL_R_MISSING_SUPPORTED_GROUPS_EXTENSION).

boundaries.mechanism: application callback reentrancy: client_hello_cb, servername_cb, alpn_select_cb, ticket_key_cb, msg_callback
residuals: client_hello_cb must not free or invalidate s; SSL_CLIENT_HELLO_RETRY is a wait boundary with no resumption.
servername_cb and alpn_select_cb must not free s; on SSL_TLSEXT_ERR_OK the selected ALPN pointer is readable for selected_len.
msg_callback must not free s; the message buffer is stack-local for the duration of the call.

boundaries.mechanism: certificate flight DER encoding: tls13_construct_certificate, tls12_construct_certificate
residuals: write_handshake_message frames at most 17000 bytes, so a certificate-flight body larger than 16996 bytes is refused; the authority's WPACKET is unbounded. This pre-existing reduced boundary is now explicit and safe.
The chain stack must contain live X509 objects; every DER blob is sized first and encoded into an exact reservation.
ticket_key_cb must initialise the supplied cipher/HMAC contexts; iv_len > EVP_MAX_IV_LENGTH and MAC length > EVP_MAX_MD_SIZE are now refused rather than overflowing.
A context without ticket_key_cb suppresses ticket construction (the reduced default-key boundary).
Decryption reads key_name(16) and the IV from etick; the callback must not retain those pointers.

boundaries.mechanism: ephemeral key exchange and signature construction: tls12_construct_server_key_exchange, tls12_sign, tls12_verify, tls13_construct_cert_verify
residuals: The active certificate slot's privatekey must be a live signing key able to produce the selected scheme.
EVP_MD_CTX/EVP_PKEY owners are released exactly once on success and every refusal arm.

boundaries.mechanism: record read/write and drivers: tls12_read_handshake, tls12_write_change_cipher_spec, tls12_server_drive, tls13_server_drive, server_wait
residuals: A failure poisons the connection through ossl_statem_fatal plus rwstate; there is no rollback to a reusable pre-message state (authority parity).
pending_cipher is assumed non-NULL at two TLS1.3 driver sites; it is set by tls_process_client_hello and is unreachable unset from the public entry.

boundaries.mechanism: session creation and PSK resumption ownership: ssl_get_new_session calls, tls13_decrypt_ticket result adoption, ssl_update_cache
residuals: A looked-up session is either transferred to the connection or freed exactly once on the rejection arm.
Session internals in ssl_sess.rs (rank 61) remain deferred and block family graduation.

boundaries.mechanism: bounded message construction: server hello (TLS1.2/1.3), encrypted extensions, certificate request, CCS, Finished
residuals: Every body is built in a fixed buffer after explicit length checks (server hello 96, EE 514, cert request 256, SKE 2048, Finished 12).

defects.description: tls13_construct_certificate encoded the leaf with i2d_X509 into der[0u8; 8192] and checked derlen > der.len() only afterwards. i2d_X509 with a non-NULL out-pointer writes the whole DER and has no capacity argument, so a certificate >= 8192 bytes overflowed the stack buffer.
defects.fix: Size first with i2d_X509(cert, NULL), compute body_len with checked_add, allocate the body through OwnedBuf, and encode into the exact reservation.

defects.description: tls12_construct_certificate encoded the leaf into der[0u8; 8192] and each chain certificate into a fresh d2[0u8; 8192], checking the length only after each write; the 8300-byte body was also fixed. A certificate or chain element >= 8192 bytes overflowed the stack.
defects.fix: Two-pass construction: size every DER blob with i2d_X509(x, NULL), sum with checked_add, allocate the exact body through OwnedBuf, then encode each certificate into its reservation.

defects.description: construct_stateless_ticket reserved 32 bytes for the HMAC tail, but ticket_key_cb chooses the HMAC digest; HMAC_Final writes the digest length (up to EVP_MAX_MD_SIZE = 64). A SHA-384/512 callback overflowed the Vec. The authority reserves EVP_MAX_MD_SIZE (statem_srvr.c:4314-4317).
defects.fix: Reserve EVP_MAX_MD_SIZE in the ticket capacity (checked_add chain) and refuse hlen > EVP_MAX_MD_SIZE before truncate.
defects.regression: source/authority differential; the affected srvr ticket probe and the full SSL member-buffer probe set were re-run

defects.class: panic / authority over-read on a contract-violating cipher IV length
defects.description: After ticket_key_cb, iv_len was cast to usize and used to slice iv[..iv_len] without bounding it by EVP_MAX_IV_LENGTH. A callback installing a cipher with a longer IV made the slice panic (caught by guard_ffi) after the callback had already written into the 16-byte iv buffer.
defects.fix: Refuse iv_len > EVP_MAX_IV_LENGTH with the suppression path.
defects.regression: covered by the ticket probe and source review; a dedicated long-IV callback control is NOT_RUN

defects.class: leak on a constructor refusal arm
defects.description: SSL_new allocated the DTLS state before CRYPTO_new_ex_data, but the ex_data refusal branch ran the authority's bare-block teardown (lock + block only) at ssl_lib.c:731, which skipped the destructor and leaked d1. The authority allocates d1 only after ossl_ssl_init succeeds.
defects.fix: dtls1_free(s) on the ex_data refusal branch before the lock/block release.
defects.regression: source/authority ordering differential; not reachable through the current DTLS court (allocator-refusal control NOT_RUN)

defects.description: The supportedgroups copy used supportedgroups_len * size_of::<u16>() without checked_mul. The only writer, tls1_set_groups, bounds the length to 64, so no reachable overflow exists; the standard nevertheless requires the checked form for an allocation extent.
defects.fix: checked_mul; an unrepresentable product refuses the SSL_new allocation path.
defects.regression: source review; no reachable input exists to drive the overflow arm

relocated: The two unbounded i2d_X509 writes moved from fixed stack buffers to exact reservations derived from a first sizing pass (the i2d FFI call remains unsafe and now has a valid extent contract).
The TLS1.3 ticket MAC write moved from a 32-byte tail inside a Vec to an EVP_MAX_MD_SIZE reservation, matching the authority's WPACKET reservation.
unsafe_accounting.behavior_delta: Certificate flights now allocate their body through OwnedBuf/CRYPTO_malloc at (NULL, 0) and refuse a body > 16996 bytes; the old port used stack buffers (and overflowed above 8192). Tickets accept SHA-384/512 ticket_key_cb digests safely and refuse iv_len > 16. SSL_new releases d1 on the ex_data refusal path and refuses an unrepresentable supportedgroups byte extent.
unsafe_accounting.safe_caller_ub: none known: every exported entry point in both files is unsafe extern C with a stated contract or a private helper reached from one; the safe interior helpers (MemberBufSlot::clear, refcount accessors, read-only getters) do not accept raw pointers. The repaired oversize paths are covered by safe test callers only through the internal unsafe test helpers.
